Posterior of the rate ratio from blinded event counts of several studies

Source: R/multibin_post.R
multibin_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of a rate ratio common to several blinded studies from the total numbers of subjects with the event in each study, with the Bayesian model of Goren et al. (2020).

Usage

multibin_post(
  y,
  n,
  k = 1,
  prior_c,
  lrr_prior = c(0, 5),
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Numbers of subjects with the event, one per study.

n

Numbers of enrolled subjects, one per study.

k

Randomization ratios of study drug to control, one per study or one for all.

prior_c

Shape parameters of the Beta prior of the control probabilities: c(a, b) for all studies, or a matrix with one row c(a_s, b_s) per study.

lrr_prior

Mean and standard deviation c(m, v) of the normal prior of \(\log \delta\); the default is that of Goren et al. (2020).

rr0

Critical value of the rate ratio.

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible interval.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles are not computed (they are NA).

control

List of settings of the numerical integration: n_coarse (default 41), n_v (Chebyshev points, default 49), n_theta (Gauss-Legendre nodes per panel of the integral over each control probability, default 12), check (default TRUE), eps (default 1e-8) and max_iter (default 12).

Value

An object of class bssd_post with model "MULTIBIN", prob, signal, rr (posterior median and credible interval of \(\delta\); the mean is NA), estimates (posterior mean of \(\log \delta\)), labels and settings, data, prior and integration.

Details

Study \(s\) has \(N_s\) enrolled subjects, \(Y_s\) subjects with the event, and the probability \(r_s = k_s / (k_s + 1)\) of study drug. The model is $$Y_s \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(N_s, \theta_s (1 - r_s + r_s \delta)), \quad \theta_s \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a_s, b_s), \quad \log \delta \sim N(m, v^2),$$ restricted to \(\theta_s \le 1 / \delta\), so that the study drug probability \(\delta \theta_s\) is at most 1. The control probabilities \(\theta_s\) may differ between studies, and \(\delta\) is common. Given \(\delta\), each \(\theta_s\) is integrated out by composite Gauss-Legendre quadrature on \(\mathrm{logit}(\theta_s)\) over the region where the integrand is not negligible, so the posterior of \(\delta\) is one-dimensional. A coarse grid locates the posterior mass in \(z = (\log \delta - m) / v\), and the posterior is integrated at Chebyshev points of \(z\) or of the prior distribution function \(\Phi(z)\), whichever represents the density more accurately (integration$coordinate); \(z\) is used when the data conflict with an informative prior of \(\log \delta\). Goren et al. (2020) sample the same posterior by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

A signal is declared when \(P(\delta > rr_0 \mid \mathrm{data}) > \) cutoff. With a single study, the likelihood is that of binbeta_post with \(\theta_d = \delta \theta_c\).

The posterior mean of \(\delta\) is not reported, because with the vague prior recommended by Goren et al. (2020) (\(v = 5\)) it depends on the far right tail of the prior; the posterior median and the credible interval are reported instead, and estimates holds the posterior mean of \(\log \delta\).

References

Goren, E., Lin, L.-A., Blaustein, R. O. and Ball, G. (2020). Bayesian meta-analysis of safety outcomes using blinded clinical trial data. Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science, 54, 1557–1565. doi:10.1007/s43441-020-00183-7

Examples

# four studies with randomization 1:1 and a control prior with mean 0.02
multibin_post(y = c(6, 10, 25, 47), n = c(200, 400, 800, 1600), k = 1,
              prior_c = c(2, 98))
#> Model: MULTIBIN 
#> Tested quantity: rate ratio delta common to the studies
#> P(delta > 1 | data) = 0.7692
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of delta: median 1.675, 95% interval (0.1729, 5.239)
